answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry for a fixed period before it may vote or claim rewards. One operator can still create many identities, but each raven in the flock ties up capital, and reclaiming it requires waiting; a gale of cheap accounts therefore becomes expensive and slow. The registry can use a cipher-based commitment to bind each deposit to one identity without exposing the owner, while audits prevent reuse of the same locked token.
